messages:
sophia: Hey team, saw intermittent ssl.SSLError on our python async service after we rotated the custom CA for the Dedicated VPC endpoint. Using the Async client with base_url pointed at the dedicated host and a corporate HTTP proxy. Some requests succeed, others fail with:

    ssl.SSLError: [SSL: CERTIFICATE_VERIFY_FAILED] certificate verify failed (_ssl.c:xxxx)

sophia: Repro steps: deploy app, keep AsyncClient alive across cert rotation, rotate CA on the dedicated endpoint, then call generate() a few times. Failures start showing up after rotation.
aj: Is your client passing a ca_bundle path or an ssl_context? Which HTTP lib underneath (httpx/aiohttp)? Also confirm whether connections are pooled/kept alive.
sophia: We're using the official py SDK (async) which uses httpx under the hood in our runtime. We set ca_bundle='/etc/certs/company-ca.pem' and proxies={'https': 'http://proxy:3128'}. We do NOT recreate the client between rotations.
aj: Likely root cause: the transport's SSLContext is created once and caches trustroots. Replacing the file on disk doesn't mutate the in-memory SSLContext. Workarounds: 1) Recreate the AsyncClient after rotation; 2) disable keepalive so new connections read the bundle.
kevin: Confirmed on infra: our cert rotation is atomic (rename into place) but clients that keep TLS sessions open will keep using old roots. Quick mitigation: make app reload the client process on SIGHUP or expose a small endpoint to call that recreates the SDK client.
kevin: Also, you can tune httpx transport to avoid keepalive: httpx.AsyncHTTPTransport(retries=1, pool_limits=httpx.Limits(max_keepalive_connections=0)) — forces new TLS handshakes per request (perf impact). For aiohttp, create a TCPConnector with keepalive_timeout=0 and recreate the session.
olga: Security gotcha: if you implement auto-reload for CA files, ensure updates are atomic (write+rename) and file perms are strict. Avoid partial reads while swapping files. Also audit KMS references to old certs.
sophia: Would it make sense for the SDK to offer a convenience flag like reload_truststore=True so users don't have to build hacks? Opening an issue with a repro in a small container that demonstrates the file-swap behavior.
aj: Yes, please open an issue. For the SDK change we could accept either a boolean to re-init transports on demand or a hook that the app calls. For async processes, a lightweight API: client.reload_truststore() that recreates the transport/connector. That avoids a full process restart.
kevin: Infra can also emit a post-rotate webhook so apps can subscribe and call client.reload_truststore or hit a reload endpoint behind a process manager. We'll coordinate with platform ops if you want that pattern supported in docs.
devex-bot: Created issue #4327: "py-sdk(async): support client.reload_truststore() or transport hot-reload for Dedicated/VPC custom CA rotations" — https://git.internal/redwood/track/4327 :robot_face:
aj: Implementation notes: need tests for httpx and aiohttp transports, ensure no resource leak when swapping connectors, and document perf tradeoffs. Also consider a TTL-based re-check for file changes as an alternative to explicit reload calls.
olga: Please add a short paragraph to the Dedicated onboarding docs about the proxy + custom CA combination: recommend atomic cert writes, signal-based reloads, avoid in-place file edits, and an example using process SIGHUP to recreate clients.
sophia: Thanks everyone — I'll try the pool-disable workaround and add a SIGHUP handler to recreate AsyncClient for now. I'll attach logs and a minimal repro to #4327 once I validate. :thumbsup:
